channel.title: Math paradoxes
channel.description: The Monty Hall problem, the birthday paradox and other puzzles where intuition fails. Play them, run simulations and follow clear explanations.

item.title: Four auctions
item.description: Four smart buyers, four auction formats: first price, second price, English and Dutch. Which brings the seller the most on average?
item.content:encoded: Four smart buyers, four auction formats: first price, second price, English and Dutch. Which brings the seller the most on average?

media:content.media:description: Four auction formats, first price, second price, English and Dutch, with the question of which brings in more.

item.title: The elevator paradox
item.description: A lift runs non-stop between floors 1 and 15; you are on floor 2 and walk out to it at a random moment. Is the first lift more often going up, down, or both equally?
item.content:encoded: A lift runs non-stop between floors 1 and 15; you are on floor 2 and walk out to it at a random moment. Is the first lift more often going up, down, or both equally?

media:content.media:description: A 15-storey building, a lift in its shaft and a person on floor 2. Which way will the first lift to arrive be going: up or down?

item.title: The broken stick
item.description: A stick is broken at two random points, chosen independently. What is the chance the three pieces make a triangle?
item.content:encoded: A stick is broken at two random points, chosen independently. What is the chance the three pieces make a triangle?

media:content.media:description: A wooden stick with two breaks and its three pieces. What is the chance they make a triangle?

item.title: Hats in the cloakroom
item.description: A cloakroom attendant hands the guests' hats back at random. What is the chance that nobody gets their own? And how does it change with 100 guests instead of 10?
item.content:encoded: A cloakroom attendant hands the guests' hats back at random. What is the chance that nobody gets their own? And how does it change with 100 guests instead of 10?

media:content.media:description: A row of guests and a pile of hats in a cloakroom. What is the chance that nobody gets their own hat?

item.title: The ant on a rubber rope
item.description: An ant crawls 1 cm/s along a 1 km rope, and every second the rope is stretched by another kilometre. Will it ever reach the end?
item.content:encoded: An ant crawls 1 cm/s along a 1 km rope, and every second the rope is stretched by another kilometre. Will it ever reach the end?

media:content.media:description: A rubber rope with an ant by the post. The rope grows a kilometre every second, the ant crawls a centimetre. Will it reach the end?

item.title: The prosecutor's fallacy
item.description: Blood at a burglary matches the defendant. Such a match occurs in one adult in 10,000, and the city has 500,000 adults. How likely is he to be innocent?
item.content:encoded: Blood at a burglary matches the defendant. Such a match occurs in one adult in 10,000, and the city has 500,000 adults. How likely is he to be innocent?

media:content.media:description: A town of dots with one person ringed: their blood matched a 1 in 10,000 trace. How likely is it that they are innocent?

item.title: The traveler's dilemma
item.description: Two broken vases; each owner writes a price from $2 to $100. Both get the lower one, with a $2 bonus for writing it. What would you write?
item.content:encoded: Two broken vases; each owner writes a price from $2 to $100. Both get the lower one, with a $2 bonus for writing it. What would you write?

media:content.media:description: Two broken vases and two price cards marked with question marks. Which number from 2 to 100 would you write?

item.title: Axelrod's tournament
item.description: Programs play the prisoner's dilemma for 200 rounds, each against each. Who scores most: an eternal defector, a sneak, Tit for Tat or a coin toss?

item.title: Parrondo's paradox
item.description: Game A loses. Game B loses. What happens to your money if before each round you pick one of them at random?

item.title: Hilbert's hotel
item.description: A hotel has infinitely many rooms, all taken. One more guest arrives. Is there a room for them if nobody may be thrown out?

item.title: The fly between two trains
item.description: Two trains 100 km apart head toward each other at 50 km/h, and a fly shuttles between them at 75 km/h. How far does it fly before the trains meet?
item.content:encoded: Two trains 100 km apart head toward each other at 50 km/h, and a fly shuttles between them at 75 km/h. How far does it fly before the trains meet?

item.title: Peeking at an A/B test
